analysis.title: Mkt upside, NVDA & ASML excellent buying
key_insights: UBS tactical teams see equities and risk assets as exhausted to the downside. Rebecca Cheong (US equity derivatives tactical strategist) says the anticipated weakness is close to over ahead of the Thursday IPO, unless more cyber attacks and outages trigger further retail anxiety and unwind.
Cheong's work shows large IPOs create a pre-launch liquidity drought that reverses after launch. SPX averages -5.8% in the 3 weeks before an IPO and +9.5% in the following 3 months.

Fast-money positioning is washed out. UBS PB L/S net exposure is near a 5-year low, and Risk Control, CTA and leveraged ETF exposures sit at the 2nd, 5th and 11th percentile versus 1 year. Cheong says an intraday -2% drawdown no longer has the quant feedback loop to become -4% on the same day.

Jason Perl (UBS tactical strategist, Knowledge Network) recommends buying equities with SPX upside toward 8,485. He expects lower VIX and MOVE, lower oil and lower rates. Only 14% of US stocks are overbought, against 18% oversold.

Perl argues oil and yields are peaking for normalization reasons, not recession fears. REITs, homebuilders, airlines and HY and IG credit are not behaving as they would heading into a recession, similar to 2022 into 2023. 20.28% of the S&P is already down more than 10%, versus 26.84% when the 10-year yield was 5.36%, so yield-sensitive names have already derated.

Perl is constructive on biotech, communication services, cyber security, healthcare, homebuilders, industrials, semis, software, tech, transportation and utilities. He is more cautious on energy, media, banks, travel and leisure, and autos.

Hansen concludes the sell-off may end soon and that semis are a good place to look for upside reversals. He calls Nvidia and ASML sector sentiment drivers and says both offer excellent entry points today.

NVDA (Buy): UBS stays constructive on semis despite post-midterm challenges and possible export restrictions on a few EM countries. UBS estimates such restrictions could remove 1-2GW of demand, about 10% of compute demand, at roughly $30bn+ of hardware per GW.

Risk to NVDA: it may change its vendor financing strategy. Colette has been more restrictive than Jensen on this, so a change is possible if she stays on as CEO. Tim Arcuri cut his 2028 profit estimates by 10% for over-ordering risk.

Support for NVDA: the US datacenter build pipeline was always heavily discounted in analyst estimates, so a midterm-driven curtailment has leeway before it hits consensus profits. UBS also says more than half of Semi sector AI exposure is already implicitly discounted.

Hansen disagrees with sales colleague Darren, who wants analysts to cut estimates more aggressively before buying semis. He cites SOX underperforming SPX by close to 30% since mid June and says one should not wait too long to buy NVDA and AI/datacenter names.

HOLT shows NVDA with over 500% upside to fair value even if profits and cash flow fade gradually. The stock trades at 8.7x Jan-28 EPS with a 9% equity free cash flow yield, and revenue is growing above 70%.
NVDA Q3 results beat consensus and matched the higher buy-side bogey, with revenue growth of 103%, EBIT +115% and EPS +111%. UBS raised 2027 top-line growth from +70% to +75%.

ASML (Buy): Francois Bouvignies's latest note covers the MATCH Act, which looks more likely to be enacted. China is about 20% of ASML sales in 2026, estimated at 25% in 2027 and 10% in 2028, and half of that is immersion tools.

UBS says only part of the China immersion market is at risk because the MATCH Act details point to more granular restrictions. The impact would be below the worst case and manageable after the sell-off and lower multiple. ASML's US and Japan peers have heavier China exposure, yet ASML's historical valuation premium to them has been eradicated.

ASML trades on 19.5x 2027 EPS with double-digit profit growth, a net cash balance sheet and significant cash flow capacity. The shares price in over half of AI profits disappearing in the coming years.

tension_points.bull_case: Hansen says NVDA and the broader AI/datacenter names should be bought now. SOX has underperformed SPX by close to 30% since mid June, multiples are very attractive, and more than half of semi AI exposure is already implicitly discounted.
tension_points.bear_case: UBS Tech Spec sales colleague Darren is waiting for analysts to cut estimates more aggressively to de-risk the sector names before a more durable share price upside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further export restrictions removing 1-2GW of demand, or a change in NVDA's vendor financing strategy that triggers deeper earnings cuts.

tension_points.bull_case: Washed-out CTA, retail and fast-money positioning, the post-IPO liquidity reversal and expected lower VIX, MOVE, oil and rates support upside toward SPX 8,485.
tension_points.bear_case: Further cyber attacks and outages could trigger more retail anxiety and unwind, and external shocks could hit risk assets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: More cyber attacks and outages that keep triggering retail anxiety and unwind before the Thursday IPO.

theme_stances.key_argument: Discounted datacenter pipeline and implicit expectations already pricing in recent risks make risk/reward attractive.
Only part of China immersion sales is at risk, so the impact is less than the worst case and manageable.
